title: "Is early-onset colorectal cancer rising in the Netherlands?"
date: "2026-10-24"
format:

Early-onset colorectal cancer has risen markedly in many Western countries among cohorts born since the 1950s and 60s [@siegelColorectalCancerIncidence2017; @sungColorectalCancerIncidence2025]. However, not everyone is immediately convinced of such statistics: a priori you should probably believe that many increases reflect changes in data collection processes rather than genuine changes in disease burden; greater diagnostic scrutiny, evolving case definitions, and the introduction of screening can all increase _recorded_ incidence without any true rise in disease. The Netherlands may provide useful information to separate artefact from reality here. Its cancer registry, the Netherlands Cancer Registry (NKR), run by [IKNL](https://iknl.nl/nkr), has covered the whole country[^reg-coverage] since 1989 and, crucially, makes their detailed, up-to-date, and historical data openly available through an API. I use those data here in two ways: to examine trends in the Netherlands, and to shed broader light on artefacts in early-onset colorectal cancer incidence figures.

[^reg-coverage]: You may be surprised to learn how many countries do not have a national cancer registry: France, the USA, Australia, Canada to name a few! 

::: {.callout-note .key-findings title="At a glance"}
::: {.kf-section}
**The trend**

- Under 50, the incidence of colon and rectum cancer rose by **1.2% a year** over the past 30 years, and by **1.0% a year** over the past 10.
- The rise appears steeper in men than in women (**+1.3%** against **+1.1%** a year over 30 years, **+1.4%** against **+0.6%** over 10).
- The rise is in the colon (**+1.5% a year** over 30 years, **+2.3%** over 10); rectal cancer rose more slowly over 30 years (**+0.8%**) and fell over the last 10 (**-1.0%**).
- At 40-44, people born around 1975 had a **40%** higher incidence than people born around 1960 had at the same age, and a **25%** higher death rate.
- From 50 onwards the picture is the reverse: since screening began in 2014, incidence at 50-74 has fallen below its 1989 level. Screening can save(s) (your) live(s)!
- The vast majority of cases still occurs later in life: **95%** of the colon and rectum cancers in 2020-24 were diagnosed at 50 or older.
:::

::: {.kf-section}
**Is it real?**

- Neuroendocrine tumours and the appendix were excluded from the analysis and do not contribute to these numbers. Based on these Dutch numbers, a registry that does include these would show a steeper rise under 50: **+1.6%** a year over 30 years instead of **+1.2%**, and **+1.4%** over 10 instead of **+1.0%**.
- It's unlikely screening contributes to this rise as no one under 55 is invited, and the rise began long before 2014.
- The rise is also not caused by a greater diagnosis of small tumours: under 50, stage IV rose by **2.3% a year** over the past 30 years and by **1.1%** over the past 10, while stage I barely changed (**+0.3%** and **+0.5%**).
- Contrary to incidence, deaths under 50 have not risen (**-0.3%** a year since 1996, **-1.6%** over the past 10; over 10 years **-3.6%** in women and **+0.3%** in men). However, five-year survival at 18-44 went from **55%** for patients diagnosed in 1990-94 to **66%** in 2015-19, though it has not improved since 2005-09 (**67%**). This makes the decrease in deaths per year over the past 10 years harder to attribute to a real increase in disease burden.
:::
:::

# Data
To comprehensively describe the trends in colorectal cancer for the Netherlands, I use three sources:

- **Incidence and survival:** NKR-cijfers. They provide incidence cases per year, sex and five-year age group from 1989 to 2024 for the colon, the appendix, and the rectosigmoid and rectum (C19-C20). Importantly, they do not only provide this by site, but also by morphology such that we can separate colorectal carcinomas from neuroendocrine tumours of the digestive tract (more on why that is important later). Moreover, they provide detailed stage and relative survival information. The most recent year with data available, 2025, is still provisional, and I leave it out.
- **Deaths:** the WHO mortality database, which holds the causes of death of Statistics Netherlands (CBS) at four ICD-10 characters, from 1996 -- the first year the Netherlands coded its deaths in ICD-10.
- **Population:** CBS StatLine.[^pop]

# Describing the trends

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| code-summary: "Code: packages, figure theme and colours"
#| code-fold: show
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)

# The figures are SVG, so they stay sharp at any size and zoom. Cairo's svg()
# rather than svglite: it writes the text as outlines, as a PDF would, where
# svglite leaves it to the browser, which draws rotated text -- the y-axis
# titles -- unevenly. The outlines also carry the font, whatever the reader has.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dev = "svg")

# What nl-data.R expects to find; it stops if one is missing
NL_FIRST_YEAR        <- 1989L   # the NKR starts in 1989, WHO's ICD-10 deaths in 1996
NKR_KEEP_PRELIMINARY <- FALSE   # the NKR's latest year (2025) is provisional
N_AGEGRP             <- 18L     # five-year age groups 0-4 ... 85+
sex_labels           <- c("Men", "Women")
ua_handle <- function() curl::new_handle(
  useragent = "R/quarto (blog post on colorectal cancer in the Netherlands)")

APPENDIX <- "C181"   # the appendix, in the cases and in the deaths
SEXES    <- c("Persons", "Men", "Women")

# The figures follow the house style of a manuscript of mine on the same
# question: Financial Times-like, one colour per outcome, grey for context, few
# lines, and panel titles set like headings. The type is larger than in print,
# for a figure read at the width of a blog column; TEXT is the size of the
# labels drawn inside a figure, in mm.
FIG_FONT <- intersect(c("Liberation Sans", "Arial", "Helvetica"),
                      systemfonts::system_fonts()$family)[1]
if (is.na(FIG_FONT)) FIG_FONT <- "sans"

COL <- c(Incidence = "#0F5499", Mortality = "#990F3D", context = "#6B6560",
         ink = "#33302E", grid = "#E9E4DF", axis = "#66605C")
TEXT <- 3.3

theme_ft <- function(grid = c("y", "x", "xy"), base_size = 11) {
  grid <- match.arg(grid)
  line <- element_line(colour = COL[["grid"]], linewidth = if (grid == "xy") 0.2 else 0.3)
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size, base_family = FIG_FONT) +
    theme(
      text               = element_text(colour = COL[["ink"]]),
      axis.text          = element_text(colour = COL[["axis"]], size = rel(0.95)),
      axis.title         = element_text(colour = COL[["axis"]], size = rel(0.95)),
      axis.ticks         = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = if (grid != "y") line else element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = if (grid != "x") line else element_blank(),
      strip.text         = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0, size = rel(1.1),
                                        colour = COL[["ink"]], margin = margin(b = 3)),
      plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0, size = rel(1.1),
                                        colour = COL[["ink"]], margin = margin(b = 3)),
      plot.title.position = "panel",
      panel.spacing.x    = unit(5, "mm"),
      panel.spacing.y    = unit(4, "mm"),
      legend.position    = "top",
      legend.justification = "left",
      legend.location    = "plot",
      legend.title       = element_blank(),
      legend.text        = element_text(size = rel(1), colour = COL[["ink"]]),
      legend.key.spacing.x = unit(4, "mm"),
      legend.margin      = margin(0, 0, 2, 0),
      plot.margin        = margin(2, 3, 2, 2, "mm"))
}

# A colour taken part of the way to black: the shade of a trend line, dark
# enough to stand apart from the points it runs through
shade <- \(x, by = 0.45) colorRampPalette(c(x, "black"))(101)[round(by * 100) + 1]

# One figure per tab, tabs nested in tabs: `levels` holds the tabs of each
# level, outermost first, and `make()` draws the figure of one tab of each
# level, taking them in that order -- or a list of figures, drawn one under
# the other. Written into the page, so the chunk that
# calls it needs `results: asis`.
tab_figures <- function(levels, make, chosen = list()) {
  depth <- length(chosen) + 2
  for (x in levels[[1]]) {
    cat("\n\n", strrep("#", depth), " ", x, "\n\n", sep = "")
    if (length(levels) > 1) {
      cat("::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n")
      tab_figures(levels[-1], make, c(chosen, x))
      cat("\n\n:::\n\n")
    } else {
      figs <- do.call(make, c(chosen, x))
      for (f in if (inherits(figs, "gg")) list(figs) else figs) {
        print(f)
        cat("\n\n")
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| label: nl-data
```

```{r}
#| label: rates
#| code-summary: "Code: age-specific and age-standardised rates"
#| code-fold: show
# Segi (1960) world standard population, per 100,000, for the 18 age groups
SEGI <- c(12000, 10000, 9000, 9000, 8000, 8000, 6000, 6000, 6000, 6000,
          5000, 4000, 4000, 3000, 2000, 1000, 500, 500)
age_label <- \(g) if_else(g == 18, "85+", str_c((g - 1) * 5, "-", (g - 1) * 5 + 4))

# Cases (or deaths) and population per sex, year and age group for a set of
# codes, with Persons added. The codes share a population, so they are summed
# within a sex first; men and women do not, so Persons adds their populations.
by_sex <- function(d, codes = unique(d$code)) {
  s <- d |>
    filter(code %in% codes) |>
    summarise(cases = sum(cases), pop = first(pop), .by = c(sex, year, agegrp))
  bind_rows(s,
            s |>
              summarise(cases = sum(cases), pop = sum(pop), .by = c(year, agegrp)) |>
              mutate(sex = "Persons")) |>
    mutate(sex = factor(sex, SEXES))
}

# The age-standardised rate per 100,000 over the age groups `ages`, per sex
# and year
asr <- function(d, ages) {
  d |>
    filter(agegrp %in% ages) |>
    mutate(w = SEGI[agegrp] / sum(SEGI[ages])) |>
    summarise(rate = sum(w * cases / pop) * 1e5, cases = sum(cases), .by = c(sex, year)) |>
    arrange(sex, year)
}

# Colon and rectum: the NKR's two groups, so the appendix and the NETs are out
CRC <- c("C18 excl. C181", "C19-C20")
inc <- list(
  `Colon and rectum` = by_sex(inc_codes, CRC),
  Colon              = by_sex(inc_codes, "C18 excl. C181"),
  Rectum             = by_sex(inc_codes, "C19-C20"),
  Appendix           = by_sex(inc_codes, APPENDIX),
  NET                = by_sex(net_codes))
mort     <- by_sex(mort_codes |> filter(code != APPENDIX))
# The deaths split as the cases: the colon is C18 without the appendix, the
# rectum C19-C20
SITES  <- c("Colon and rectum", "Colon", "Rectum")
DEATHS <- list(`Colon and rectum` = mort,
               Colon  = by_sex(mort_codes |> filter(str_starts(code, "C18"), code != APPENDIX)),
               Rectum = by_sex(mort_codes |> filter(code %in% c("C19", "C20"))))
mort_c26 <- by_sex(bind_rows(mort_codes |> filter(code != APPENDIX),
                             c26_codes |> filter(code == "C260")))
# The share of those deaths certified as C26.0, over the age groups `ages` and
# the years `years`
c26_share <- function(ages, years) {
  n <- \(d) sum(d$cases[d$agegrp %in% ages & d$year %in% years])
  100 * n(filter(c26_codes, code == "C260")) / n(filter(mort_c26, sex == "Persons"))
}

# A number in the text: rounded, with a thousands separator
fmt <- \(x, digits = 1) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")

# The check against the NKR's own world-standardised rate: all ages, both
# sexes, and the appendix in, as in the NKR's own colorectal group
wsr_check <- asr(by_sex(inc_codes), 1:18) |>
  filter(sex == "Persons") |>
  inner_join(nl_nkr$published |>
               filter(measure == "incidence WSR, C18-C20, persons") |>
               select(year, wsr = value), by = "year") |>
  mutate(diff = 100 * (rate / wsr - 1))
wsr_check_max <- max(abs(wsr_check$diff))
stopifnot("the age-standardised rate no longer reproduces the NKR's own to 0.05%" =
            wsr_check_max < 0.05)
```

</details>

[^pop]: CBS StatLine offers an "average population" by age (*gemiddelde bevolking*), which seems the obvious choice. But in that table CBS counts people by the age they reach during the year, which is half a year older than the age at diagnosis or death that the NKR and WHO count. Against those counts it shifts people into older age groups, and makes an age-standardised rate about 2% too low. I use the mean of the population on 1 January of the year and on 1 January of the next year, at the same age, instead.

Below, I plot the mortality and incidence series for early onset (20-49) and later onset (50-74)[^ages] and estimate the annual percentage change (EAPC) by fitting a straight line through the logarithm of the yearly rates and turning the slope estimate into percentage change per year.

[^ages]: Leaving out the youngest and oldest ages is common in descriptive cancer epidemiology as under 20, colorectal cancer is very rare and from 75 on, the data tend to be less reliable (in some registries): older people with other illnesses are less often investigated down to a confirmed diagnosis, and their causes of death are harder to pin down. 50-74 also matches up with the ages that the Dutch screening programme invites (55-75).

```{r}
#| label: eapc
#| code-summary: "Code: fit the EAPCs and draw the trends figure"
# The EAPC as in my report (and Rcan::csu_eapc): a straight line through the
# log of the yearly rates over the last `n` years of a series, whose slope b
# becomes a percentage change per year, 100 * (exp(b) - 1); the 95% interval
# is b +/- 1.96 standard errors. A year with no cases has no log rate and is
# left out of the fit, and with fewer than three years left there is no fit.
# `keys` are the columns that tell one series from another.
WINDOWS <- c(`Past 10 years` = 10L, `Past 30 years` = 30L)

eapc <- function(d, n, keys = "sex") {
  d |>
    mutate(window_to = max(year), window_from = window_to - n + 1L,
           .by = all_of(keys)) |>
    filter(year >= window_from) |>
    nest(.by = all_of(c(keys, "window_from", "window_to"))) |>
    mutate(years_zero = map_int(data, \(x) sum(x$rate == 0)),
           fit = map(data, \(x) {
             x <- filter(x, rate > 0)
             if (nrow(x) < 3)
               return(tibble(eapc = NA_real_, low = NA_real_, up = NA_real_,
                             intercept = NA_real_, slope = NA_real_,
                             year_from = NA_real_, year_to = NA_real_))
             m  <- summary(lm(log(rate) ~ year, data = x))$coefficients
             b  <- m["year", "Estimate"]
             se <- m["year", "Std. Error"]
             tibble(eapc = 100 * (exp(b) - 1),
                    low  = 100 * (exp(b - qnorm(0.975) * se) - 1),
                    up   = 100 * (exp(b + qnorm(0.975) * se) - 1),
                    intercept = m["(Intercept)", "Estimate"], slope = b,
                    year_from = min(x$year), year_to = max(x$year))
           })) |>
    select(-data) |>
    unnest(fit)
}

# The EAPC of an age-standardised rate over the age groups `ages`, both sexes
# unless asked for one, as it is quoted in the text
band_eapc <- function(d, ages, window, sex = "Persons") {
  eapc(asr(d, ages), WINDOWS[[window]]) |> filter(sex == !!sex)
}
# Numbers in the text: the estimate in bold, its interval not
fmt_eapc <- \(r) sprintf("**%+.1f%%** a year (95%% CI %+.1f to %+.1f)", r$eapc, r$low, r$up)
fmt_e    <- \(r) sprintf("**%+.1f%%**", r$eapc)

BAND_AGES <- list(`Early onset, 20-49` = 5:10, `Later onset, 50-74` = 11:15)

trend <- imap(list(Incidence = inc[SITES], Mortality = DEATHS), \(sites, outcome)
  imap(sites, \(d, site) imap(BAND_AGES, \(a, b) asr(d, a) |> mutate(band = b)) |>
         list_rbind() |> mutate(site = site)) |>
    list_rbind() |> mutate(outcome = outcome)) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(band = factor(band, names(BAND_AGES)))

trend_fit <- imap(WINDOWS, \(n, w) eapc(trend, n, keys = c("outcome", "site", "band", "sex")) |>
                    mutate(window = w)) |>
  list_rbind()

# A rate in the text: one outcome, band and year, both sexes, colon and rectum
# unless asked for one
trend_at <- function(outcome, band, yr, site = "Colon and rectum") {
  trend$rate[trend$outcome == outcome & trend$band == band & trend$sex == "Persons" &
               trend$site == site & trend$year == yr]
}
trend_eapc <- \(outcome, band, window, sex = "Persons", site = "Colon and rectum") trend_fit |>
  filter(outcome == !!outcome, band == !!band, window == !!window, sex == !!sex,
         site == !!site)

# Two y axes per panel: incidence on the left, mortality on the right. The
# right-hand axis runs to twice the highest death rate of any sex and site, so
# that the deaths run along the lower half of the panel and the cases along
# the upper, and each axis is the same in every tab; `k` turns a death rate into the
# left-hand scale.
nice_top <- \(x) max(pretty(c(0, x)))
AXES <- trend |>
  summarise(top = max(rate), .by = c(outcome, band)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = outcome, values_from = top) |>
  mutate(left = map_dbl(Incidence, nice_top), right = map_dbl(2 * Mortality, nice_top),
         k = left / right)

# Annual rates as points joined by a pale line, the trend over the window as a
# dashed line in a darker shade, and its EAPC at the line's end -- as in the
# manuscript's time series. The EAPC label also names its series, in the colour
# of that series' axis, so there is no legend to look up. The start of
# screening is marked where it applies.
# Years on the x axis: the decades, and in smaller type the first and last
# year of the window. A size per label is not officially supported by
# ggplot2, and warns, but works.
# In narrower panels, `gap` leaves out the decades that close to a window year.
window_years <- \(window) max(trend$year) - c(WINDOWS[[window]] - 1L, 0L)
trend_years  <- function(window, gap = 0) {
  w <- window_years(window)
  decades <- seq(1990, max(trend$year), 10)
  sort(c(keep(decades, \(y) all(abs(y - w) > gap)), w))
}

fig_trends <- function(window, sex, site) {
  panels <- map(levels(trend$band), \(b) {
    ax    <- filter(AXES, band == b)
    on_ax <- \(outcome, y) if_else(outcome == "Mortality", y * ax$k, y)
    d   <- trend |>
      filter(band == b, sex == !!sex, site == !!site) |>
      mutate(y = on_ax(outcome, rate))
    fit <- trend_fit |> filter(band == b, sex == !!sex, site == !!site, window == !!window)
    seg <- fit |>
      mutate(year = map2(year_from, year_to, \(a, z) seq(a, z, length.out = 25))) |>
      unnest(year) |>
      mutate(y = on_ax(outcome, exp(intercept + slope * year)))
    lab <- fit |>
      mutate(year = year_to, y = on_ax(outcome, exp(intercept + slope * year_to)),
             label = str_c(outcome, "\n", sprintf("%+.1f%%/yr", eapc)))
    screen <- if (b == "Later onset, 50-74")
      list(geom_vline(xintercept = 2013.5, colour = COL[["context"]], linetype = "dotted",
                      linewidth = 0.45),
           annotate("text", x = 2013.5, y = ax$left, label = "Screening starts\n(FIT, 55-75)",
                    hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1, size = TEXT * 0.9, colour = COL[["context"]],
                    family = FIG_FONT, lineheight = 0.95))

    ggplot(d, aes(year, y, colour = outcome)) +
      screen +
      geom_line(linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.35) +
      geom_point(size = 0.9) +
      geom_line(data = seg, aes(colour = str_c(outcome, " trend")), linewidth = 0.8,
                linetype = "62", show.legend = FALSE) +
      # ggrepel: in the rectum the two labels can end at the same height
      ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = lab, aes(label = label, colour = outcome), hjust = 0,
                               nudge_x = 0.8, direction = "y", xlim = c(max(d$year) + 0.5, Inf),
                               size = TEXT, fontface = "bold", family = FIG_FONT,
                               lineheight = 0.9, segment.colour = NA,
                               min.segment.length = Inf, box.padding = 0.15, seed = 1) +
      scale_colour_manual(
        values = c(COL[c("Incidence", "Mortality")],
                   `Incidence trend` = alpha(shade(COL[["Incidence"]]), 0.85),
                   `Mortality trend` = alpha(shade(COL[["Mortality"]]), 0.85)),
        guide = "none") +
      scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, ax$left), breaks = pretty(c(0, ax$left)),
                         expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.03)),
                         name = "Incidence per 100,000 (age-standardised)",
                         sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / ax$k, breaks = pretty(c(0, ax$right)),
                                             name = "Mortality per 100,000 (age-standardised)")) +
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = trend_years(window),
                         expand = expansion(add = c(1, 11))) +
      coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
      labs(title = b, x = NULL) +
      theme_ft("xy") +
      theme(axis.text.x        = element_text(
              size = rel(if_else(trend_years(window) %in% window_years(window), 0.75, 1)),
              vjust = 1),
            axis.ticks.x       = element_line(colour = COL[["axis"]], linewidth = 0.3),
            axis.ticks.length.x = unit(1.2, "mm"),
            axis.text.y.left   = element_text(colour = COL[["Incidence"]]),
            axis.title.y.left  = element_text(colour = COL[["Incidence"]]),
            axis.text.y.right  = element_text(colour = COL[["Mortality"]]),
            axis.title.y.right = element_text(colour = COL[["Mortality"]]))
  })
  wrap_plots(panels, nrow = 1)
}
```

:::

As you can see, colorectal carcinomas show very different trends between late and early onset. The rollout of FIT screening (a test for blood in the stool, at 55-75y) at first found many more cancers, after which incidence dropped sharply: screening had brought diagnoses forward, and removed polyps before they could turn into cancer. Early-onset colorectal cancer, on the other hand, is rising, mostly in the colon: there the rise was steeper over the past 10 years than over the past 30, while rectal cancer turned down. Trends also appear to be steeper among men.

Next, let's look if there's variation within these age groups. 

```{r}
#| label: eapc-age
#| code-summary: "Code: EAPCs per five-year age group, and their figure"
AGE_GROUPS <- 5:18   # 20-24 ... 85+
FIT_KIND <- c("Every year had cases", "Some years had no cases")

# The cases (or deaths) behind each fit: all of them in the window's years
window_cases <- \(d, n) d |>
  filter(year > max(year) - n) |>
  summarise(cases = sum(cases), .by = c(sex, agegrp))

age_fit <- imap(list(Incidence = inc[SITES], Mortality = DEATHS), \(sites, outcome)
  imap(WINDOWS, \(n, w)
    imap(sites, \(d, site) {
      d <- d |>
        filter(agegrp %in% AGE_GROUPS) |>
        mutate(rate = cases / pop * 1e5)
      eapc(d, n, keys = c("sex", "agegrp")) |>
        left_join(window_cases(d, n), by = c("sex", "agegrp")) |>
        mutate(site = site)
    }) |>
      list_rbind() |>
      mutate(window = w)) |>
    list_rbind() |>
    mutate(outcome = outcome)) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(site = factor(site, SITES),
         age  = factor(age_label(agegrp), rev(age_label(AGE_GROUPS))),
         fit  = factor(if_else(years_zero > 0, FIT_KIND[2], FIT_KIND[1]), FIT_KIND))

age_eapc_at <- \(site, age, window, sex = "Persons", outcome = "Incidence") age_fit |>
  filter(site == !!site, age == !!age, window == !!window, sex == !!sex,
         outcome == !!outcome)

# The same axis in every tab, so the sexes and the windows compare; an
# interval that runs past it ends in an arrowhead, and an EAPC past it sits on
# its edge with its value written next to it
EAPC_XLIM <- c(-10, 10)

# An age group per row, the youngest at the top; in each row the cases above
# and the deaths below, with their number in the window just right of the
# panel. Each EAPC is written by its point, the cases' above and the deaths'
# below. Dashed lines mark off 20-49 and 50-74. A fit that had to leave out a
# year without a single case is drawn hollow: such fits are pulled toward no
# change, as the years left out are the lowest.
fig_age_eapc <- function(window, sex, site) {
  xlim <- EAPC_XLIM
  d <- age_fit |>
    filter(window == !!window, sex == !!sex, site == !!site, !is.na(eapc)) |>
    mutate(y    = as.integer(age) + if_else(outcome == "Incidence", 0.17, -0.17),
           x    = pmin(pmax(eapc, xlim[1]), xlim[2]),
           lo_c = pmax(low, xlim[1]), hi_c = pmin(up, xlim[2]))
  under50   <- sum(levels(d$age) %in% age_label(5:10))
  over74    <- sum(levels(d$age) %in% age_label(16:N_AGEGRP))
  arrow_end <- arrow(length = unit(1, "mm"), type = "closed", angle = 25)
  whisker   <- \(...) geom_segment(..., linewidth = 0.4)
  off_axis  <- filter(d, abs(eapc) > xlim[2])

  ggplot(d, aes(y = y, colour = outcome)) +
    annotate("segment", x = xlim[1], xend = xlim[2],
             y = c(length(levels(d$age)) - under50, over74) + 0.5,
             colour = COL[["context"]], linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = COL[["ink"]], linewidth = 0.45) +
    whisker(aes(x = x, xend = lo_c, yend = y), data = \(x) filter(x, low >= xlim[1])) +
    whisker(aes(x = x, xend = lo_c, yend = y), data = \(x) filter(x, low < xlim[1], x > lo_c),
            arrow = arrow_end) +
    whisker(aes(x = x, xend = hi_c, yend = y), data = \(x) filter(x, up <= xlim[2])) +
    whisker(aes(x = x, xend = hi_c, yend = y), data = \(x) filter(x, up > xlim[2], x < hi_c),
            arrow = arrow_end) +
    # show.legend = TRUE: without it, a kind of fit the tab does not have gets
    # an empty key
    geom_point(aes(x = x, shape = fit), fill = "white", size = 1.8, stroke = 0.6,
               show.legend = TRUE) +
    geom_text(data = off_axis, aes(x = x, label = sprintf("%+.0f", eapc),
                                   hjust = if_else(eapc > 0, 1, 0)),
              nudge_x = if_else(off_axis$eapc > 0, -0.8, 0.8), size = TEXT * 0.85,
              family = FIG_FONT, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_text(aes(x = x, label = sprintf("%+.1f", eapc),
                  vjust = if_else(outcome == "Incidence", -0.9, 1.8)),
              data = \(x) filter(x, abs(eapc) <= xlim[2]), size = TEXT * 0.65,
              family = FIG_FONT, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_text(aes(x = xlim[2], label = fmt(cases, 0)), hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.9,
              size = TEXT * 0.75, family = FIG_FONT, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(xlim[1], xlim[2], 2),
                       labels = \(x) if_else(x > 0, str_c("+", x), as.character(x))) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq_along(levels(d$age)), labels = if_else(levels(d$age) == "85+", ">84y", str_c(levels(d$age), "y")),
                       expand = expansion(add = 0.6)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = COL[c("Incidence", "Mortality")]) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = set_names(c(19, 21), FIT_KIND), drop = FALSE) +
    guides(shape = guide_legend(order = 2, override.aes = list(colour = COL[["ink"]]))) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = xlim, clip = "off") +
    labs(x = str_c("Estimated annual percentage change (%), ", str_to_lower(window)),
         y = NULL) +
    theme_ft("x") +
    theme(plot.margin = margin(5, 30, 5, 5))
}
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6.4
#| echo: false
tab_figures(list(names(WINDOWS), SEXES, SITES), fig_age_eapc)
```

:::

We see that over the past 30 years, colon and rectum cancer became more common in every early-onset age group. Over the past 10 years the picture is a bit noisier. In the colon, incidence rose in most early-onset age groups, but not at 30-34. For colon and rectum together several age groups were flat, 50-54 among them, while the slightly older screened age groups fell, most steeply from 60 on.

## Same age, different generations
Instead of plotting trends per age group and diagnosis, we can also inspect the data by looking at people from the same age across different birth cohorts: how does colorectal cancer differ across generations? Is a 44y old born in 1975 at more risk than one born in 1960?

```{r}
#| label: aspr
#| code-summary: "Code: rates per birth cohort, and the cohort figure"
# Rates per age group in 5-year windows: a window sits at the middle of its
# years, and an age group in it holds, on average, the people born that
# window's middle minus the age group's middle -- 40-44 in 1990-94 is the people
# born around 1950. The report's age-specific rates. The windows are counted
# back from the last year, so that every one holds five years: 1990-94 to
# 2020-24 for the cases, and 2000-04 to 2020-24 for the deaths, which start in
# 1996.
ASPR_AGES <- 5:15   # 20-24 ... 70-74
aspr_rates <- function(d, ages = ASPR_AGES) {
  last  <- max(d$year)
  start <- last - 5L * ((last - min(d$year) + 1L) %/% 5L) + 1L
  d |>
    filter(year >= start, agegrp %in% ages) |>
    mutate(window = start + 5L * ((year - start) %/% 5L)) |>
    summarise(cases = sum(cases), py = sum(pop), .by = c(sex, window, agegrp)) |>
    mutate(rate       = cases / py * 1e5,
           period_mid = window + 2.5,
           cohort     = period_mid - ((agegrp - 1) * 5 + 2.5),
           age        = factor(age_label(agegrp), age_label(ASPR_AGES)))
}
aspr <- aspr_rates(inc$`Colon and rectum`)

# The deaths from 25-29 up: under 25 there are a handful in a window, and none
# at all in some windows of one sex, which a log scale cannot show
ASPR <- list(Incidence = aspr, Mortality = aspr_rates(mort, 6:15))
stopifnot("an age group of the deaths has a window without a death" =
            all(ASPR$Mortality$cases > 0))

# Two birth cohorts at the same age: their rates and the ratio of the later to
# the earlier, with the usual interval for a ratio of two Poisson rates
cohort_ratio <- function(age, then, now, sex = "Persons", d = aspr) {
  a <- d |> filter(age == !!age, cohort == then, sex == !!sex)
  b <- d |> filter(age == !!age, cohort == now, sex == !!sex)
  rr <- b$rate / a$rate
  se <- sqrt(1 / a$cases + 1 / b$cases)
  tibble(rate_then = a$rate, rate_now = b$rate, rr = rr,
         lo = rr * exp(-1.96 * se), hi = rr * exp(1.96 * se))
}
fmt_rr  <- \(r) sprintf("**%.2f** (95%% CI %.2f-%.2f)", r$rr, r$lo, r$hi)
fmt_pct <- \(r) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * (r$rr - 1))

# The cohorts compared at HIGHLIGHT, the same for both outcomes: the deaths
# start too late for people born around 1950 to be seen at 40-44
COHORTS   <- list(Incidence = c(1960, 1975), Mortality = c(1960, 1975))
HIGHLIGHT <- "40-44"

# Under 50 in shades of the outcome's colour, the older age groups in grey; both
# darkest next to 50 and fading away from it. The age group whose cohorts are
# compared is drawn heavier.
age_col <- \(outcome) set_names(
  c(colorRampPalette(c(c(Incidence = "#9DBCE0", Mortality = "#E0A3B8")[[outcome]],
                       COL[[outcome]]))(6),
    colorRampPalette(c(COL[["context"]], "#CFC9C3"))(5)),
  age_label(ASPR_AGES))

# The same axes in every tab: the rates of both outcomes and all sexes, with
# room at the top for the cohort labels, and the years of both outcomes
ASPR_ALL <- list_rbind(ASPR)
ASPR_Y   <- range(ASPR_ALL$rate) * c(1, 1.6)
ASPR_X   <- list(cohort = range(ASPR_ALL$cohort), period_mid = range(ASPR_ALL$period_mid))

# One panel: a line per age group against `x`. The compared cohorts' points at
# HIGHLIGHT are circled, and in the birth-year panel (`marks`) also labelled.
# `breaks` and `labels` go to the x axis.
aspr_half <- function(d, x, x_lab, outcome, marks = NULL,
                      breaks = scales::breaks_width(10), labels = waiver()) {
  ends  <- d |> slice_max({{ x }}, by = age)
  stars <- d |> filter(age == HIGHLIGHT, cohort %in% COHORTS[[outcome]])
  star_labels <- if (!is.null(marks))
    geom_label(data = stars, aes(label = str_c("born ", cohort, ": ", fmt(rate))),
               vjust = -0.6, size = TEXT * 0.9, fontface = "bold", family = FIG_FONT,
               fill = alpha("white", 0.85), linewidth = 0, label.padding = unit(0.4, "mm"),
               show.legend = FALSE)
  ggplot(d, aes({{ x }}, rate, group = age, colour = age)) +
    marks +
    geom_line(aes(linewidth = age == HIGHLIGHT)) +
    geom_point(size = 1.1) +
    geom_point(data = stars, size = 3, shape = 21, fill = "white", stroke = 1) +
    star_labels +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = ends, aes(label = age), hjust = 0, direction = "y",
                             nudge_x = 1.5, size = TEXT * 0.85, family = FIG_FONT,
                             segment.colour = NA, min.segment.length = Inf, seed = 1,
                             show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = age_col(outcome), guide = "none") +
    scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 0.45, `TRUE` = 1.1), guide = "none") +
    scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200),
                  labels = \(x) format(x, drop0trailing = TRUE, trim = TRUE)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = breaks, labels = labels,
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.12))) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = ASPR_X[[as_label(enquo(x))]], ylim = ASPR_Y) +
    labs(x = x_lab, y = NULL) +
    theme_ft("y")
}

# A 5-year window by its middle, written over two lines: "1990" over "-94"
window_label <- \(mid) str_c(mid - 2.5, "\n-", str_sub(mid + 1.5, 3, 4))

fig_aspr <- function(outcome, sex) {
  d  <- ASPR[[outcome]] |> filter(sex == !!sex)
  co <- COHORTS[[outcome]]
  cohort_marks <- list(
    geom_vline(xintercept = co, colour = COL[["context"]], linetype = "dotted",
               linewidth = 0.45),
    annotate("label", x = co, y = ASPR_Y[2], label = str_c("born ", co),
             size = TEXT * 0.9, colour = COL[["context"]], family = FIG_FONT,
             fill = "white", linewidth = 0, label.padding = unit(0.6, "mm"), vjust = 1))
  (aspr_half(d, cohort, "Year of birth", outcome, cohort_marks) +
     labs(y = str_c(outcome, " per 100,000 (age-specific, log scale)"))) +
    (aspr_half(d, period_mid,
               if (outcome == "Mortality") "Year of death" else "Year of diagnosis", outcome,
               breaks = sort(unique(ASPR_ALL$period_mid)), labels = window_label) +
       theme(axis.ticks.x = element_line(colour = COL[["axis"]], linewidth = 0.3),
             axis.ticks.length.x = unit(1.2, "mm"),
             axis.text.x = element_text(size = rel(0.8), lineheight = 0.9))) +
    plot_layout(widths = c(1.7, 1))
}
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| echo: false
tab_figures(list(names(ASPR), SEXES), fig_aspr)
```

:::

If we read along the 40-44 line, we see that people born around 1975 had a rate of **`r fmt(cohort_ratio("40-44", 1960, 1975)$rate_now)`** per 100,000 at 40-44, `r fmt_rr(cohort_ratio("40-44", 1960, 1975))` times the **`r fmt(cohort_ratio("40-44", 1960, 1975)$rate_then)`** of people born around 1960 at the same age. Their death rate at 40-44 was **`r fmt(cohort_ratio("40-44", 1960, 1975, d = ASPR$Mortality)$rate_now)`** per 100,000, `r fmt_rr(cohort_ratio("40-44", 1960, 1975, d = ASPR$Mortality))` times the **`r fmt(cohort_ratio("40-44", 1960, 1975, d = ASPR$Mortality)$rate_then)`** of people born around 1960.

### APC model
We can also investigate this using a statistical model. Namely, we can fit an age-period-cohort (APC) model that fits the incidence data as a function of age (higher risk of cancer with age), period (something in a particular period changed and affected everyone), and birth cohort (affected only people born in year $x$). Below, I fit one to colorectal cancer incidence and mortality at 20-54y. I exclude the >54y groups because screening has introduced a stark period effect there.

Notably, APC models are, at its core, unidentifiable as knowing two of age, calendar period and birth cohort determines the other: birth year = calendar year - age. This means that the data cannot separate the linear parts of the three effects; a steady rise over time could mean that each calendar year is riskier than the last (period effect), or that each generation is riskier than the one before (cohort effect), or any mix of the two. All of these combinations fit the data equally well!

However, departures from straight lines (e.g. a bump) and the sum of the straight-line period and cohort (drift) terms _are_ identifiable. Following @downhamIncreaseEarlyonsetColorectal2025, I assume there is no linear period trend and assign all of the drift to the cohorts. The period curve then shows only deviations from a straight line (e.g. the bumps), while the cohort curve shows the overall rise (the sum) and the cohort bumps.

```{r}
#| label: apc
#| code-summary: "Code: fit the age-period-cohort models, and their figure"
# Poisson APC models as in Downham et al. (2025), with Epi::apc.fit: drift
# given to the cohorts (parm = "ACP"), B-splines with 5 degrees of freedom per
# term (model = "bs": natural splines are linear past their outer knots, which
# flattens just the most recent cohorts), cohort rate ratios relative to people
# born in 1960, and period effects without trend. Unlike Downham et al., A is
# the middle of the age group and P the middle of the 5-year window, so a
# cohort P - A is the mean year of birth in it, as in the cohort figure, and 1960 is
# one of them. The windows are those of the cohort figure: 1990-94 to 2020-24 for the
# cases, 2000-04 to 2020-24 for the deaths.
APC_AGES <- 5:11   # 20-24 ... 50-54, the ages never invited for screening
APC_REF  <- 1960
apc_table <- function(d, ages = APC_AGES) {
  last  <- max(d$year)
  start <- last - 5L * ((last - min(d$year) + 1L) %/% 5L) + 1L
  d |>
    filter(agegrp %in% ages, year >= start) |>
    mutate(A = (agegrp - 1) * 5 + 2.5, P = start + 5 * ((year - start) %/% 5) + 2.5) |>
    summarise(D = sum(cases), Y = sum(pop), .by = c(sex, A, P))
}
# apc.fit prints the degrees of freedom it uses whatever it is told; kept quiet
apc_fit <- function(x) {
  fit <- NULL
  invisible(capture.output(
    fit <- Epi::apc.fit(as.data.frame(x), ref.c = APC_REF, parm = "ACP",
                        dist = "poisson", model = "bs", npar = 5, print.AOV = FALSE)))
  fit
}
APC_DATA <- list(Incidence = inc[SITES], Mortality = DEATHS)
apc_fits <- expand_grid(outcome = names(APC_DATA), site = SITES, sex = SEXES) |>
  mutate(table = pmap(list(outcome, site, sex), \(o, st, sx)
                   apc_table(APC_DATA[[o]][[st]]) |> filter(sex == sx) |> select(-sex)),
         fit   = map(table, apc_fit))

# The cohort and period effects as rate ratios with their 95% intervals
apc_effects <- apc_fits |>
  mutate(eff = map(fit, \(f) bind_rows(
    Cohort = as_tibble(f$Coh, .name_repair = \(n) c("x", "rr", "low", "up")),
    Period = as_tibble(f$Per, .name_repair = \(n) c("x", "rr", "low", "up")),
    .id = "term"))) |>
  select(outcome, site, sex, eff) |>
  unnest(eff)
apc_rr <- \(cohort, outcome = "Incidence", site = "Colon and rectum", sex = "Persons")
  apc_effects |>
    filter(term == "Cohort", x == cohort, outcome == !!outcome, site == !!site, sex == !!sex)
fmt_rr1 <- \(r) sprintf("**%.2f** (95%% CI %.2f-%.2f)", r$rr, r$low, r$up)

# Per fit: the net drift, the yearly change the model leaves to the cohorts,
# and the tests of the cohort effect beyond the drift and of the period effect
# beyond the cohorts
apc_tests <- apc_fits |>
  mutate(drift = map(fit, \(f) 100 * (unname(as.numeric(f$Drift[1, ])) - 1)),
         p_cohort = map_dbl(fit, \(f) f$Anova[3, "Pr(>Chi)"]),
         p_period = map_dbl(fit, \(f) f$Anova[4, "Pr(>Chi)"])) |>
  transmute(outcome, site, sex,
            drift_low = map_dbl(drift, \(x) x[2]), drift_up = map_dbl(drift, \(x) x[3]),
            drift = map_dbl(drift, \(x) x[1]), p_cohort, p_period)

# What the data can say without the model: the rate of a cohort against that
# of people born in 1960 at the ages both were seen at, in the same table the
# model is fitted to. Pooled over those ages with the Mantel-Haenszel rate
# ratio and the Greenland-Robins variance of its log. A cohort that shares no
# age with 1960 has no observed ratio: its modelled one is extrapolation, on
# the assumption that a cohort's effect is the same at every age.
mh_rr <- function(D1, Y1, D0, Y0) {
  t <- Y1 + Y0
  r <- sum(D1 * Y0 / t)
  s <- sum(D0 * Y1 / t)
  se <- sqrt(sum(Y1 * Y0 * (D1 + D0) / t^2) / (r * s))
  tibble(rr = r / s, low = rr * exp(-1.96 * se), up = rr * exp(1.96 * se))
}
apc_observed <- function(table, cohort) {
  d <- table |> mutate(C = P - A)
  both <- inner_join(filter(d, C == cohort), filter(d, C == APC_REF),
                     by = "A", suffix = c("1", "0"))
  if (nrow(both) == 0)
    return(tibble(ages = "none", n_ages = 0L, rr = NA_real_, low = NA_real_, up = NA_real_))
  bind_cols(tibble(ages = str_c(min(both$A) - 2.5, "-", max(both$A) + 1.5),
                   n_ages = nrow(both)),
            with(both, mh_rr(D1, Y1, D0, Y0)))
}
APC_COMPARE <- c(1970, 1980, 1990, 2000)
apc_compare <- apc_fits |>
  filter(sex == "Persons") |>
  mutate(cmp = map(table, \(t) map(APC_COMPARE, \(c) apc_observed(t, c) |> mutate(cohort = c)) |>
                     list_rbind())) |>
  select(outcome, site, cmp) |>
  unnest(cmp) |>
  left_join(apc_effects |> filter(term == "Cohort", sex == "Persons") |>
              select(outcome, site, cohort = x, model = rr, model_low = low, model_up = up),
            by = c("outcome", "site", "cohort"))
# Per outcome, the cohorts that share at least one age with 1960: the span of
# the curve the data can check, drawn solid in the APC figure
apc_checked <- apc_fits |>
  filter(site == "Colon and rectum", sex == "Persons") |>
  mutate(span = map(table, \(t) {
    cs <- sort(unique(t$P - t$A))
    ok <- cs[map_int(cs, \(c) apc_observed(t, c)$n_ages) > 0]
    tibble(from = min(ok), to = max(ok))
  })) |>
  select(outcome, span) |>
  unnest(span)
apc_obs <- \(cohort, outcome = "Incidence", site = "Colon and rectum") apc_compare |>
  filter(cohort == !!cohort, outcome == !!outcome, site == !!site)

# The cases and the deaths in one plot per sex and site, on one log axis, the
# same in every tab; the bands of the latest cohorts' deaths run past it, and
# are cut off there
APC_YLIM <- c(0.25, 8)

# One panel: a line and its 95% band per outcome, named at its right-hand end.
# `solid` is the part of each line drawn solid over a dashed one; the legend
# says what the two mean, and is left out where there is nothing dashed
LINE_KIND <- c(solid  = "Compared with 1960 at an age both were seen at",
               dashed = "Extrapolated by the model")
apc_panel <- function(d, title, breaks, labels = waiver(), solid = d) {
  ends <- d |> slice_max(x, by = outcome)
  ggplot(d, aes(x, rr, colour = outcome, fill = outcome)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = COL[["axis"]], linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = low, ymax = up), colour = NA, alpha = 0.15) +
    geom_line(aes(linetype = LINE_KIND[["dashed"]]), linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_line(aes(linetype = LINE_KIND[["solid"]]), data = solid, linewidth = 0.8) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = set_names(c("solid", "22"), LINE_KIND),
                          breaks = unname(LINE_KIND),
                          guide = if (nrow(solid) < nrow(d))
                            guide_legend(override.aes = list(colour = COL[["ink"]], fill = NA,
                                                             linewidth = 0.6))
                          else "none") +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = ends, aes(label = outcome), hjust = 0, nudge_x = 1,
                             direction = "y", size = TEXT * 0.9, fontface = "bold",
                             family = FIG_FONT, segment.colour = NA,
                             min.segment.length = Inf, seed = 1) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = COL[c("Incidence", "Mortality")], guide = "none") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = COL[c("Incidence", "Mortality")], guide = "none") +
    scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8),
                  labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = breaks, labels = labels,
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.16))) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = APC_YLIM) +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_ft("y") +
    theme(axis.ticks.x = element_line(colour = COL[["axis"]], linewidth = 0.3),
          axis.ticks.length.x = unit(1.2, "mm"))
}
fig_apc <- function(sex, site) {
  d <- apc_effects |> filter(site == !!site, sex == !!sex)
  coh_d <- filter(d, term == "Cohort")
  # solid where a cohort shares an age with 1960, dashed where it is extrapolation
  checked <- coh_d |>
    inner_join(apc_checked, by = "outcome") |>
    filter(between(x, from, to))
  coh <- apc_panel(coh_d, "Year of birth", seq(1940, 2000, 10), solid = checked) +
    annotate("point", x = APC_REF, y = 1, shape = 21, size = 2.4, fill = "white",
             colour = COL[["ink"]]) +
    labs(y = "Rate ratio at 20-54 (log scale)")
  per <- apc_panel(filter(d, term == "Period"), "Period, without its trend",
                   sort(unique(d$x[d$term == "Period"])), window_label) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = rel(0.8), lineheight = 0.9))
  coh + per + plot_layout(widths = c(1.7, 1))
}
```

::: {.panel-tabset}
```{r}
#| label: apc-tabs
#| results: asis
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4
#| echo: false
tab_figures(list(SEXES, SITES), fig_apc)
```
:::

:::

Per this model, people born around 1990 had `r fmt_rr1(apc_rr(1990))` times the incidence of people born in 1960, at the same age and in the same period. The cohort curve is flat for the people born in the 1940s and 1950s and rises in both sexes from the mid-1960s on, more in the colon (`r fmt_rr1(apc_rr(1990, site = "Colon"))`) than in the rectum (`r fmt_rr1(apc_rr(1990, site = "Rectum"))`), whose cohort curve does not depart clearly from the straight drift (p = `r fmt(filter(apc_tests, outcome == "Incidence", site == "Rectum", sex == "Persons")$p_cohort, 2)`). Mortality barely changed between the people born in 1960 and around 1980 for colorectal (`r fmt_rr1(apc_rr(1980, "Mortality"))`), but rose in the rectum: `r fmt_rr1(apc_rr(1980, "Mortality", "Rectum"))`. Age-period-cohort analyses of Australia, Canada, England and the US find the same rise in the generations born since 1960, only much steeper [@downhamIncreaseEarlyonsetColorectal2025].

We need to be a bit careful here though as this model relies on extrapolation: people born around 1990 and in 1960 were both seen at `r apc_obs(1990)$ages` only, where the observed incidence ratio is `r fmt_rr1(apc_obs(1990))`, against the model's **`r fmt(apc_rr(1990)$rr, 2)`**; people born around 1980 shared `r apc_obs(1980)$n_ages` age groups with them (`r apc_obs(1980)$ages`) (observed `r fmt_rr1(apc_obs(1980))`, modelled `r fmt_rr1(apc_rr(1980))`); while people born around 2000 were seen only at 20-24, an age the 1960 cohort was never seen at in these data, so their rate ratio of **`r fmt(apc_rr(2000)$rr, 2)`** is fully extrapolated by the model.

The model does this by assuming that risk rises with age in the same way for every generation, and that a later generation simply has all its rates multiplied by one number: its cohort effect. If people born in 1980 have, say, 1.4 times the rate of people born in 1960 at 30-44, the model assumes they also have 1.4 times the rate at 20-24 and at 50-54. That lets it compare the 2000 and 1960 cohorts at 20-24, despite the data never observing the 1960 cohort at that age: it estimates the rate the 1960 cohort would have had at 20-24 from how much lower rates at 20-24 are than at older ages in the generations that were seen at both. 

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Observed and modelled rate ratios"}
```{r}
#| label: apc-table
#| code-summary: "Code: observed and modelled rate ratios, and the model tests"
# Both sexes: each cohort against 1960, observed at the ages both were seen at
# and modelled
apc_compare |>
  transmute(outcome, site, born = cohort, `ages shared with 1960` = ages,
            observed = if_else(is.na(rr), "-", sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", rr, low, up)),
            modelled = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", model, model_low, model_up)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrlrr",
               caption = str_c("Rate ratio against people born in 1960 (95% CI), both sexes, 20-54 ",
                               "years: observed, pooled over the ages both cohorts were seen at ",
                               "(Mantel-Haenszel), and modelled. - No age in common."))

apc_tests |>
  transmute(outcome, site, sex,
            `net drift, % a year` = sprintf("%+.1f (%+.1f to %+.1f)", drift, drift_low, drift_up),
            `cohort beyond drift, p` = format.pval(p_cohort, digits = 2, eps = 0.001),
            `period beyond cohort, p` = format.pval(p_period, digits = 2, eps = 0.001)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lllrrr",
               caption = str_c("Net drift with 95% CI, and the likelihood-ratio tests of the cohort ",
                               "effect beyond the drift and of the period effect beyond the cohort ",
                               "effect (Epi::apc.fit), 20-54 years."))
```
:::

# Could we explain away this increase?

## Is it the neuroendocrine tumours or the appendix?
Neuroendocrine tumours (NETs) of the digestive tract are mostly small, slow-growing tumours, found at colonoscopy or in an appendix removed for appendicitis. However, they have a different histology and response to treatment. Therefore, they are usually not of interest in colorectal cancer epidemiology and are usually studied separately. Importantly, changes in classification and improved imaging have resulted in sharp increases in their incidence rates [@siegelColorectalCancerStatistics2020]; in the Netherlands, the reported incidence of colorectal NETs doubled between 2006 and 2011, most of them found at colonoscopy [@kooykerChangeIncidenceCharacteristics2020]. In France, a change in how registries classify them largely explains the rise in colorectal cancer at 15-39 years, while the rate of adenocarcinoma did not change [@joosteEpidemiologicalClassificationChanges2025].

The incidence figures above include neither NETs nor appendix cancer, as NKR reports them separately. Not all registries do, however, so I think it's still useful to look at these trends.

```{r}
#| label: groups
#| code-summary: "Code: trends of the NETs, appendix and colorectal carcinomas"
GROUP_BANDS <- list(`20-34` = 5:7, `35-49` = 8:10, `50-74` = 11:15)
GROUPS <- c(`Colon and rectum` = "Colon and rectum", NETs = "NET", Appendix = "Appendix")
# Ochre and teal next to the post's blue
GROUP_COL <- set_names(c(COL[["Incidence"]], "#C98A1B", "#1B7F79"), names(GROUPS))

groups <- imap(GROUPS, \(src, g) imap(GROUP_BANDS, \(a, b) asr(inc[[src]], a) |>
                                        mutate(band = b)) |>
                 list_rbind() |> mutate(group = g)) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  filter(sex == "Persons") |>
  mutate(group = factor(group, names(GROUPS)))
group_fit <- imap(WINDOWS, \(n, w) eapc(groups, n, keys = c("group", "band", "sex")) |>
                    mutate(window = w)) |>
  list_rbind()

# A panel per age band and a line per tumour group, on one log axis: points
# joined by a pale line, the trend over the window dashed in a darker shade,
# and the group and its EAPC at the line's end, as in the trends figure. ggrepel
# keeps labels that end at the same height apart, to the right of the data.
fig_groups <- function(window) {
  d   <- groups |> filter(rate > 0)
  fit <- group_fit |> filter(window == !!window)
  seg <- fit |>
    mutate(year = map2(year_from, year_to, \(a, z) c(a, z))) |>
    unnest(year) |>
    mutate(rate = exp(intercept + slope * year))
  lab <- fit |>
    mutate(year = year_to, rate = exp(intercept + slope * year_to),
           label = str_c(str_replace(group, " and ", " and\n"), "\n",
                         sprintf("%+.1f%%/yr", eapc)))
  ggplot(d, aes(year, rate, colour = group)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.55, alpha = 0.75) +
    geom_point(data = \(x) filter(x, year == max(year)), size = 1.4) +
    geom_line(data = seg, aes(colour = str_c(group, " trend")), linewidth = 0.7,
              linetype = "62") +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = lab, aes(label = label), hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.8,
                             direction = "y", xlim = c(max(d$year) + 0.5, Inf),
                             size = TEXT, fontface = "bold", family = FIG_FONT,
                             lineheight = 0.9, segment.colour = NA,
                             min.segment.length = Inf, box.padding = 0.15, seed = 1) +
    facet_wrap(~band, nrow = 1, labeller = as_labeller(\(b) str_c("Ages ", b))) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(GROUP_COL,
                                   set_names(alpha(map_chr(GROUP_COL, shade, by = 0.35), 0.9),
                                             str_c(names(GROUP_COL), " trend"))),
                        guide = "none") +
    scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200),
                  labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = trend_years(window, gap = 5),
                       expand = expansion(add = c(1, 14))) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Rate per 100,000 (age-standardised, log scale)") +
    theme_ft("xy") +
    theme(axis.text.x         = element_text(
            size = rel(if_else(trend_years(window, gap = 5) %in% window_years(window), 0.75, 1)),
            vjust = 1),
          axis.ticks.x        = element_line(colour = COL[["axis"]], linewidth = 0.3),
          axis.ticks.length.x = unit(1.2, "mm"),
          panel.spacing.x     = unit(14, "mm"),
          plot.margin         = margin(5, 30, 5, 5))
}

# Everything a registry that counts by site alone would call colorectal cancer
# (carcinomas with the appendix, plus NETs), and the NETs' share of it in the
# first and last five years
all_morph <- by_sex(bind_rows(inc_codes, net_codes))
net_share <- function(ages, years) {
  n <- \(d) sum(d$cases[d$sex == "Persons" & d$agegrp %in% ages & d$year %in% years])
  100 * n(inc$NET) / n(all_morph)
}

# Colon and rectum with the NETs added back, and with the appendix added back
with_net <- by_sex(bind_rows(inc_codes |> filter(code != APPENDIX), net_codes))
with_app <- by_sex(inc_codes)

group_eapc <- \(group, band, window = "Past 30 years") group_fit |>
  filter(group == !!group, band == !!band, window == !!window)
```

::: {.column-page}
::: {.panel-tabset}
```{r}
#| label: groups-tabs
#| results: asis
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4
#| echo: false
for (w in names(WINDOWS)) {
  cat("\n\n## ", w, "\n\n", sep = "")
  print(fig_groups(w))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```
:::


:::

At 20-34, NETs are about as common as colorectal carcinomas: in a registry that counts every tumour of the colon and rectum, whatever its morphology, about **`r fmt(net_share(5:7, 2020:2024), 0)`%** of the cases at these ages in 2020-24 would be NETs.[^net-sites] At 35-49 their share went from **`r fmt(net_share(8:10, 1990:1994), 0)`%** in 1990-94 to **`r fmt(net_share(8:10, 2020:2024), 0)`%** in 2020-24. The appendix carcinomas rose fastest of all, `r fmt_e(band_eapc(inc$Appendix, 5:10, "Past 30 years"))` a year at 20-49 over the past 30 years, as in the US [@bleyerColonColorectalAll2025], but they are rare: **`r fmt(mean(asr(inc$Appendix, 5:10) |> filter(sex == "Persons", year >= 2020) |> pull(rate)), 2)`** per 100,000 at 20-49 in 2020-24, against **`r fmt(mean(asr(inc[["Colon and rectum"]], 5:10) |> filter(sex == "Persons", year >= 2020) |> pull(rate)), 1)`** for colon and rectum. When we add them back the 30-year EAPC under 50 goes from `r fmt_e(band_eapc(inc[["Colon and rectum"]], 5:10, "Past 30 years"))` a year to `r fmt_e(band_eapc(with_net, 5:10, "Past 30 years"))` with every NET, `r fmt_e(band_eapc(with_app, 5:10, "Past 30 years"))` with the appendix, and `r fmt_e(band_eapc(all_morph, 5:10, "Past 30 years"))` with both. Both also rose at 50-74 (`r fmt_e(group_eapc("NETs", "50-74"))` and `r fmt_e(group_eapc("Appendix", "50-74"))` a year), where the colorectal carcinomas did not (`r fmt_e(group_eapc("Colon and rectum", "50-74"))`) meaning their rise is not one of the young.

[^net-sites]: An upper bound: the NKR does not split its NET group by site, so this includes the NETs of the stomach and small bowel too.

## Is it screening?
Screening finds cancers earlier, and in its first rounds it finds cancers that would otherwise have been diagnosed years later. This is clearly illustrated by the jump in 2014-2016 in the [trends figure](#trends-figure). The Dutch programme started in 2014 and invites everyone aged 55 to 75 to do a faecal immunochemical test (FIT) at home every two years [@toeszoutendijkRealTimeMonitoringResults2017]; it was phased in by year of birth, and [2019](https://zoek.officielebekendmakingen.nl/kst-32793-508.html) was the first year in which the whole age range could be invited. No one under 55 has ever been invited. Moreover, the rise under 50 began well before 2014, and 50-54, the one five-year age group over 50 that is never invited, rose too, if only slightly (`r fmt_e(age_eapc_at("Colon and rectum", "50-54", "Past 30 years"))` a year over the past 30 years).

However, screening could still reach the under-55s indirectly, through more colonoscopies in the relatives of people with a positive test (though initially I would be skeptical of the idea that Dutch doctors would eagerly follow-up on this). It does line up with the EO age of their children and the colon EO rising slightly faster in the past 10 years (i.e. since the start of LO screening). But anything that makes doctors look more often in people without symptoms would show up as more early-stage tumours. Do we see such an increase?

## Is it more diagnosis?
If more young people were looked at -- more colonoscopies for vague symptoms, more awareness among doctors -- the extra tumours would be small and early: stage I, some stage II. A rise in advanced tumours is much harder to explain that way.[^imaging]

[^imaging]: Better imaging can move tumours from stage III to stage IV, by finding small metastases that used to go unnoticed. This may explain part of the rise in stage IV. However, this would explain the relative, not their absolute rise.

```{r}
#| label: stage
#| code-summary: "Code: fill in the hidden stage counts, stage trends and their figure"
# ---- stage, with the rows the NKR hides allocated ------------------------------
# As in my report. The NKR hides a whole year x sex x age row of its stage
# table when the row holds about ten cases or fewer: always at 20-24, mostly
# at 25-29, now and then at 30-34, never from 35 up. A hidden row's total is
# known from the incidence counts, and is split across the stages in the
# proportions of the shown rows at 20-49 of the same site, year and sex. That
# is an assumption, not data; for colon and rectum together it covers about 3%
# of the cases at 20-49, for either site alone more, as the NKR hides rows by
# their size.
STAGE_LEVELS   <- c("I", "II", "III", "IV", "Unknown")
STAGES         <- STAGE_LEVELS[1:4]
STAGE_MIX_AGES <- 5:10

stage_raw <- nl_stage$stage
stopifnot(
  "NKR has colorectal cases in stage 0 or NVT; the post assumes none" =
    all(stage_raw$cases[stage_raw$stage %in% c("0", "NVT")] %in% c(0, NA)))
stage_raw <- stage_raw |> filter(stage %in% STAGE_LEVELS)

# The incidence codes of each site, which its stages must add up to
STAGE_SITE_CODES <- list(`Colon and rectum` = CRC, Colon = "C18 excl. C181",
                         Rectum = "C19-C20")
stage_totals <- imap(STAGE_SITE_CODES, \(codes, site) inc_codes |>
  filter(code %in% codes) |>
  summarise(total = sum(cases), .by = c(year, sex, agegrp)) |>
  mutate(site = site)) |>
  list_rbind()

stage_hidden <- stage_raw |>
  summarise(hidden = all(is.na(cases)), .by = c(site, year, sex, agegrp)) |>
  filter(hidden) |>
  inner_join(stage_totals, by = c("site", "year", "sex", "agegrp"))

stage_mix <- stage_raw |>
  filter(!is.na(cases), agegrp %in% STAGE_MIX_AGES) |>
  summarise(n = sum(cases), .by = c(site, year, sex, stage)) |>
  mutate(p = n / sum(n), .by = c(site, year, sex))

stage_counts <- bind_rows(
  stage_raw |> filter(!is.na(cases)) |> mutate(imputed = FALSE),
  stage_hidden |>
    inner_join(stage_mix |> select(site, year, sex, stage, p),
               by = c("site", "year", "sex"), relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    transmute(site, year, sex, agegrp, stage, cases = total * p, imputed = TRUE))

# The parts must add up to the whole, shown rows and allocated ones alike
stopifnot("the stages do not add up to the incidence counts" =
            stage_counts |>
              summarise(n = sum(cases), .by = c(site, year, sex, agegrp)) |>
              inner_join(stage_totals, by = c("site", "year", "sex", "agegrp")) |>
              with(isTRUE(all.equal(n, total))))

# Per site, stage and sex, and both sexes added up, over the population of the
# incidence counts
stage_sexes <- stage_counts |>
  summarise(imputed = sum(cases[imputed]), cases = sum(cases),
            .by = c(site, sex, year, agegrp, stage)) |>
  (\(x) bind_rows(x, x |>
                    summarise(imputed = sum(imputed), cases = sum(cases),
                              .by = c(site, year, agegrp, stage)) |>
                    mutate(sex = "Persons")))() |>
  left_join(inc$`Colon and rectum` |> mutate(sex = as.character(sex)) |>
              select(sex, year, agegrp, pop),
            by = c("sex", "year", "agegrp")) |>
  mutate(sex = factor(sex, SEXES))

STAGE_BANDS <- list(`Early onset, 20-49` = 5:10, `Later onset, 50-74` = 11:15)
stage_asr <- expand_grid(site = SITES, stage = STAGES) |>
  pmap(\(site, stage) imap(STAGE_BANDS, \(a, b)
    asr(filter(stage_sexes, site == !!site, stage == !!stage), a) |>
      mutate(site = site, stage = stage, band = b)) |>
      list_rbind()) |>
  list_rbind()
stage_fit <- imap(WINDOWS, \(n, w)
  eapc(stage_asr, n, keys = c("site", "band", "stage", "sex")) |> mutate(window = w)) |>
  list_rbind()
stage_eapc <- \(band, stage, window, site = "Colon and rectum", sex = "Persons") stage_fit |>
  filter(band == !!band, stage == !!stage, window == !!window, site == !!site,
         sex == !!sex)

imputed_share <- \(ages, site = "Colon and rectum")
  with(filter(stage_sexes, agegrp %in% ages, site == !!site, sex == "Persons"),
       100 * sum(imputed) / sum(cases))

# The share of each band's cases in each stage, per year, and the share of
# stage III and IV over a run of years
stage_share <- imap(STAGE_BANDS, \(a, b)
  stage_sexes |>
    filter(agegrp %in% a) |>
    summarise(cases = sum(cases), .by = c(site, sex, year, stage)) |>
    mutate(share = 100 * cases / sum(cases), .by = c(site, sex, year)) |>
    mutate(band = b)) |>
  list_rbind()
advanced_share <- \(band, from, to, site = "Colon and rectum", sex = "Persons") with(
  filter(stage_share, band == !!band, site == !!site, sex == !!sex, between(year, from, to)),
  100 * sum(cases[stage %in% c("III", "IV")]) / sum(cases))

# The first year of a window, as eapc() counts it
window_from <- \(window) max(stage_asr$year) - WINDOWS[[window]] + 1L

# Stage I and II a shade darker than a fill would need, so their points and
# lines show on white too
STAGE_COL <- c(I = "#9CBDE2", II = "#6A99D0", III = "#3D72B8", IV = "#0F3F7A",
               Unknown = "#D9D4CF")

# The rate of each stage, a panel per band with its own y axis, the same in
# both windows: it runs to the highest rate or trend of the band. Points joined
# by a pale line, the trend over the window dashed in a darker shade, and its
# EAPC at the line's end, which also names the stage -- as in the trends figure. The
# dotted lines mark the 7th TNM edition, labelled at the foot of the panel,
# and at 50-74 the start of screening, labelled at the top as in the trends figure.
fig_stage <- function(window, sex, site) {
  panels <- imap(names(STAGE_BANDS), \(b, i) {
    # the axis runs to the highest rate or trend of the band in any site or sex
    fit_all <- stage_fit |> filter(band == b)
    top <- max(filter(stage_asr, band == b)$rate,
               exp(fit_all$intercept + fit_all$slope * fit_all$year_from),
               exp(fit_all$intercept + fit_all$slope * fit_all$year_to), na.rm = TRUE)
    d   <- stage_asr |>
      filter(band == b, site == !!site, sex == !!sex) |>
      mutate(stage = factor(stage, STAGES))
    fit <- fit_all |> filter(window == !!window, site == !!site, sex == !!sex)
    seg <- fit |>
      mutate(year = map2(year_from, year_to, \(a, z) c(a, z))) |>
      unnest(year) |>
      mutate(rate = exp(intercept + slope * year))
    lab <- fit |>
      mutate(year = year_to, rate = exp(intercept + slope * year_to),
             label = str_c("Stage ", stage, " ", sprintf("%+.1f%%/yr", eapc)))
    marker <- \(x, label, y, vjust) list(
      geom_vline(xintercept = x, colour = COL[["context"]], linetype = "dotted",
                 linewidth = 0.45),
      annotate("text", x = x, y = y, label = label, hjust = 1.05, vjust = vjust,
               size = TEXT * 0.9, colour = COL[["context"]], family = FIG_FONT,
               lineheight = 0.95))
    screen <- if (b == "Later onset, 50-74")
      marker(2013.5, "Screening starts\n(FIT, 55-75)", top, 1)
    ggplot(d, aes(year, rate, colour = stage)) +
      marker(2009.5, "7th TNM\nedition", 0, -0.3) +
      screen +
      geom_line(linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.35) +
      geom_point(size = 0.9) +
      geom_line(data = seg, aes(colour = str_c(stage, " trend"), group = stage),
                linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "62") +
      ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = lab, aes(label = label), hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.8,
                               direction = "y", xlim = c(max(d$year) + 0.5, Inf), size = TEXT, fontface = "bold",
                               family = FIG_FONT, segment.colour = NA,
                               min.segment.length = Inf, box.padding = 0.15, seed = 1) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = c(STAGE_COL[STAGES],
                                     set_names(map_chr(STAGE_COL[STAGES], shade, by = 0.3),
                                               str_c(STAGES, " trend"))),
                          guide = "none") +
      scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05)),
                         name = if (i == 1) "Rate per 100,000 (age-standardised)" else NULL) +
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1990, 2020, 10), expand = expansion(add = c(1, 15))) +
      coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, top), clip = "off") +
      labs(title = b, x = NULL) +
      theme_ft("xy")
  })
  wrap_plots(panels, nrow = 1)
}

# The stage mix of each band, stacked to 100%: stage IV on the baseline and III
# on it, so the advanced share reads off the axis from zero; unknown against
# the top. The years before the window are faded, and the III-IV share of its
# first and last five years is written over the middle of those years. Each
# stage is named in its layer at the start of the panel, in the faded years;
# unknown, too thin for its name, above the panel's right end, clear of its title.
fig_stage_share <- function(window, sex, site) {
  from <- window_from(window)
  to   <- max(stage_share$year)
  d <- stage_share |>
    filter(site == !!site, sex == !!sex) |>
    # geom_area stacks the first level on top
    mutate(stage = factor(stage, c("Unknown", STAGES)),
           band  = factor(band, names(STAGE_BANDS)))
  adv <- expand_grid(band = factor(names(STAGE_BANDS), names(STAGE_BANDS)),
                     end = c("first", "last")) |>
    mutate(y1    = if_else(end == "first", from, to - 4L),
           share = map2_dbl(as.character(band), y1,
                            \(b, y) advanced_share(b, y, y + 4L, site, sex)),
           year  = y1 + 2,
           label = str_c(y1, "-", str_sub(y1 + 4L, 3, 4), "\n", fmt(share, 0), "%"))
  area <- geom_area(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2)
  at   <- min(d$year) + 1
  # where geom_area put each layer, read back from the plot
  names_at <- layer_data(ggplot(d, aes(year, share, fill = stage)) + area +
                           facet_wrap(~band, nrow = 1)) |>
    filter(abs(x - at) < 1e-9) |>
    transmute(band  = factor(levels(d$band)[PANEL], levels(d$band)),
              stage = levels(d$stage)[group],
              year  = if_else(stage == "Unknown", max(d$year), min(d$year) + 0.6),
              share = if_else(stage == "Unknown", 100, (ymin + ymax) / 2),
              label = if_else(stage == "Unknown", "Unknown", str_c("Stage ", stage)))
  ggplot(d, aes(year, share, fill = stage)) +
    area +
    annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = from - 0.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "white", alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_text(data = names_at, aes(year, share, label = label,
                                   hjust = if_else(stage == "Unknown", 1, 0),
                                   vjust = if_else(stage == "Unknown", -0.4, 0.5),
                                   colour = stage == "Unknown"),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, size = TEXT * 0.85, family = FIG_FONT, fontface = "bold") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = COL[["ink"]], `TRUE` = COL[["context"]]),
                        guide = "none") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 2009.5, colour = "white", linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_label(data = adv, aes(year, share, label = label),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = -0.15, size = TEXT * 0.85, family = FIG_FONT,
               lineheight = 0.9,
               fill = alpha("white", 0.85), linewidth = 0, label.padding = unit(0.3, "mm")) +
    facet_wrap(~band, nrow = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = STAGE_COL, guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1990, 2020, 10), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 25), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "% of cases") +
    theme_ft("xy") +
    theme(panel.spacing.x = unit(8, "mm"))
}
```

::: {.panel-tabset}
```{r}
#| label: stage-tabs
#| results: asis
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.8
#| echo: false
tab_figures(list(names(WINDOWS), SEXES, SITES),
            \(w, sex, site) list(fig_stage(w, sex, site), fig_stage_share(w, sex, site)))
```
:::


:::

Under 50, stage I barely changed over the past 30 years (`r fmt_e(stage_eapc("Early onset, 20-49", "I", "Past 30 years"))` a year), while stage IV -- tumours that have already spread to distant organs -- rose by `r fmt_eapc(stage_eapc("Early onset, 20-49", "IV", "Past 30 years"))`. Stage II fell (`r fmt_e(stage_eapc("Early onset, 20-49", "II", "Past 30 years"))`) and stage III rose (`r fmt_e(stage_eapc("Early onset, 20-49", "III", "Past 30 years"))`), but that may largely be tumours moving from one to the other because of the classification changes introduced in the 7th TNM edition. Moreover,  pathologists could perhaps examine more lymph nodes now resulting in the detecting of more tumours that have reached the nodes (stage III rather than II). However, we can compare stage I and IV as they should be unaffected. In the colon over the past 10 years, the window that overlaps with screening, stage I did rise (`r fmt_e(stage_eapc("Early onset, 20-49", "I", "Past 10 years", site = "Colon"))` a year), but stage III and IV rose far faster (`r fmt_e(stage_eapc("Early onset, 20-49", "III", "Past 10 years", site = "Colon"))` and `r fmt_e(stage_eapc("Early onset, 20-49", "IV", "Past 10 years", site = "Colon"))`) -- the opposite of what more looking would do. 

Stage III and IV made up **`r fmt(advanced_share("Early onset, 20-49", 1995, 1999), 0)`%** of the cases under 50 in 1995-99, and **`r fmt(advanced_share("Early onset, 20-49", 2020, 2024), 0)`%** in 2020-24. Jooste et al. saw the same in France: under 50, metastatic adenocarcinoma rose while adenocarcinoma overall did not [@joosteEpidemiologicalClassificationChanges2025].

At 50-74 the effect of FIT screening (55-75y) is evident again: stage I jumped after its start, and over the past 10 years all stages fell, as this window starts at the peak of the first screening round.

```{r}
#| label: survival
#| code-summary: "Code: five-year relative survival, and its figure"
# Five-year relative survival from NKR-cijfers, per 5-year period of diagnosis.
# 2020-24 is left out: most of its patients have not yet been followed for
# five years, so its five-year figure rests on the few diagnosed in 2020.
SURV_FROM <- 1990L
SURV_TO   <- 2015L
surv <- nl_surv$survival |>
  filter(years == 5, between(period, SURV_FROM, SURV_TO)) |>
  mutate(period_mid = period + 2.5)
# The NKR hides the survival of some small groups of one site and sex; the
# figure leaves a gap there, but the figures quoted in the text, of colon and
# rectum and both sexes, must all be shown
stopifnot("the NKR hides a survival figure of colon and rectum, both sexes" =
            !anyNA(filter(surv, site == "Colon and rectum", sex == "Persons")$survival))
surv_at <- \(age, stage, period, site = "Colon and rectum", sex = "Persons") surv |>
  filter(age == !!age, stage == !!stage, period == !!period, site == !!site,
         sex == !!sex) |>
  pull(survival)
# The share dying of the disease within five years, last period over first
excess_ratio <- (100 - surv_at("18-44", "All", SURV_TO)) /
  (100 - surv_at("18-44", "All", SURV_FROM))

# The stages in the blues of the stage figure, all stages together in ink, heavier;
# the youngest age group in the incidence colour, 45-54 -- which straddles 50 --
# in a paler shade of it, and the older groups in grey, darkening with age
SURV_STAGE_COL <- c(All = COL[["ink"]], STAGE_COL[STAGES])
SURV_STAGE_LAB <- c(All = "All stages", set_names(str_c("Stage ", STAGES), STAGES))
SURV_AGE_COL   <- set_names(c(COL[["Incidence"]], "#7EA6D6",
                              colorRampPalette(c("#B5AEA7", COL[["context"]]))(3)),
                            unname(NKR_SURV_AGES))
SURV_PERIODS   <- seq(SURV_FROM, SURV_TO, 5L) + 2.5
# The tabs of the figure: a panel per stage, or per age group
SURV_VIEWS     <- c(stage = "By stage", age = "By age group")

# Two views of the same numbers: `by = "age"` draws a panel per age group and a
# line per stage, `by = "stage"` the reverse, with the line that stands out --
# all stages, or 18-44 -- drawn heavier. One y axis throughout; the dotted line
# marks the 7th TNM edition, as in the stage figure. Every period is named, at a
# slant and in smaller type so that they fit.
fig_survival <- function(by = c("age", "stage"), sex, site) {
  by <- match.arg(by)
  d <- surv |>
    filter(site == !!site, sex == !!sex) |>
    mutate(stage = factor(SURV_STAGE_LAB[stage], SURV_STAGE_LAB),
           age   = factor(age, unname(NKR_SURV_AGES)))
  line <- if (by == "age") "stage" else "age"
  cols <- if (by == "age") set_names(SURV_STAGE_COL, SURV_STAGE_LAB) else SURV_AGE_COL
  ggplot(d, aes(period_mid, survival, colour = .data[[line]], group = .data[[line]])) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 2010, colour = COL[["context"]], linetype = "dotted",
               linewidth = 0.45) +
    geom_line(aes(linewidth = .data[[line]] %in% c("All stages", "18-44"))) +
    geom_point(size = 1.1) +
    facet_wrap(vars(.data[[by]]), nrow = 1) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = cols) +
    scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 0.6, `TRUE` = 1.1), guide = "none") +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 25),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = SURV_PERIODS,
                       labels = \(x) str_c(x - 2.5, "-", str_sub(x + 1.5, 3, 4)),
                       expand = expansion(add = 2)) +
    labs(x = "Period of diagnosis", y = "5-year relative survival (%)") +
    theme_ft("xy") +
    theme(axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1,
                                            size = rel(0.75)),
          axis.ticks.x       = element_line(colour = COL[["axis"]], linewidth = 0.3),
          axis.ticks.length.x = unit(1, "mm"))
}
```

Another way to check the diagnosis argument is deaths. If the extra tumours were harmless, deaths would not follow. In the Dutch under 50y data, deaths have not risen ([trends figure](#trends-figure)): `r fmt_e(trend_eapc("Mortality", "Early onset, 20-49", "Past 30 years"))` a year since 1996, though rectal cancer deaths did (`r fmt_eapc(trend_eapc("Mortality", "Early onset, 20-49", "Past 30 years", site = "Rectum"))`).Over the past 10 years they fell clearly in women (`r fmt_eapc(trend_eapc("Mortality", "Early onset, 20-49", "Past 10 years", "Women"))`), but not in men (`r fmt_eapc(trend_eapc("Mortality", "Early onset, 20-49", "Past 10 years", "Men"))`). Survival, meanwhile, improved a lot (figure below). Five-year relative survival of colon and rectum cancer at 18-44 years, the NKR's youngest age group for survival, was **`r fmt(surv_at("18-44", "All", SURV_FROM), 0)`%** for patients diagnosed in 1990-94 and **`r fmt(surv_at("18-44", "All", SURV_TO), 0)`%** for those diagnosed in 2015-19, and the gain was largest in the advanced stages: at stage III from **`r fmt(surv_at("18-44", "III", SURV_FROM), 0)`%** to **`r fmt(surv_at("18-44", "III", SURV_TO), 0)`%**, and at stage IV from **`r fmt(surv_at("18-44", "IV", SURV_FROM), 0)`%** to **`r fmt(surv_at("18-44", "IV", SURV_TO), 0)`%**. More tumours, each less often fatal, can leave the death rate largely unchanged while the incidence rises. A sceptic could object that finding harmless tumours raises survival too. But stage I did not rise, and the gains were largest in stage III and IV. Most of that gain came before 2005-09, however: since then (**`r fmt(surv_at("18-44", "All", 2005), 0)`%**) survival has not improved, which leaves the past 10 years harder to explain (see below).

```{r}
tab_figures(list(SURV_VIEWS, SEXES, SITES),
```
