:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.75em; color: #6B6560;"}
NKR hides the figures for small groups, resulting in a gap in the line: `r sum(is.na(surv$survival))` of the `r nrow(surv)` figures. The NKR publishes survival only in these age groups, which differ from those in the rest of the post. A stage's survival can rise when the TNM edition moves tumours between stages (dotted line: the 7th edition, from 2010).
:::
:::


We can do some napkin math here too: if incidence rose by **`r fmt(trend_eapc("Incidence", "Early onset, 20-49", "Past 30 years")$eapc)`%** a year, and the share of patients who die of the disease within five years fell from about **`r fmt(100 - surv_at("18-44", "All", SURV_FROM), 0)`%** to **`r fmt(100 - surv_at("18-44", "All", SURV_TO), 0)`%** over the `r SURV_TO - SURV_FROM` years between those two survival periods, about **`r fmt(100 * (1 - excess_ratio^(1 / (SURV_TO - SURV_FROM))))`%** a year if spread evenly, deaths would change by about **`r fmt(100 * ((1 + trend_eapc("Incidence", "Early onset, 20-49", "Past 30 years")$eapc / 100) * excess_ratio^(1 / (SURV_TO - SURV_FROM)) - 1))`%** a year -- close to the **`r fmt(trend_eapc("Mortality", "Early onset, 20-49", "Past 30 years")$eapc)`%** a year we see.

The same sum does not work as well for the past 10 years. Incidence rose by **`r fmt(trend_eapc("Incidence", "Early onset, 20-49", "Past 10 years")$eapc)`%** a year and survival stood still, so deaths should have risen by about as much; instead they fell (`r fmt_e(trend_eapc("Mortality", "Early onset, 20-49", "Past 10 years"))` a year). Part of this may be chance, as -- fortunately -- few people under 50 die of colorectal cancer each year. Another option is the C26.0 code. These are deaths certified as "intestinal tract, part unspecified" which in practice are mostly bowel cancers whose site was not recorded. A growing share of Dutch bowel cancer deaths ends up there: at all ages it went from **`r fmt(c26_share(1:18, 1996), 0)`%** in 1996 to **`r fmt(c26_share(1:18, 2024), 0)`%** in 2024. However, under 50 it grew less, and stopped growing after the mid-2000s: **`r fmt(c26_share(5:10, 1996:2004), 0)`%** in 1996-2004, **`r fmt(c26_share(5:10, 2005:2014), 0)`%** in 2005-14 and **`r fmt(c26_share(5:10, 2015:2024), 0)`%** in 2015-24. Counting them all as colorectal cancer only gives `r fmt_e(band_eapc(mort_c26, 5:10, "Past 30 years"))` a year since 1996. So it seems that the past 10 years may in part be some (awareness) artefact.

## Is it the bookkeeping?

- **Coding.** I mentioned some coding changes already (appendix, TNM), but there's one more: CBS switched to coding causes of death automatically in 2013 ([CBS](https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/achtergrond/2014/50/verschuivingen-in-de-doodsoorzakenstatistiek-bij-de-introductie-van-het-automatisch-coderen)), which moved some deaths between codes; however the death rate under 50 was flat before and after it.
- **COVID-19.** Screening [paused for several months in 2020](https://www.rivm.nl/nieuws/minder-mensen-ontvingen-in-2020-uitnodiging-voor-bevolkingsonderzoeken-naar-kanker), and both windows include that year. Under 50, the rate in 2020 does not stand out ([trends figure](#trends-figure)).

# So, is early-onset colorectal cancer really rising in the Netherlands?
I would say so yes. Under 50, colon and rectum cancer has become more common by **`r fmt(trend_eapc("Incidence", "Early onset, 20-49", "Past 30 years")$eapc)`%** a year over the past 30 years and by **`r fmt(trend_eapc("Incidence", "Early onset, 20-49", "Past 10 years")$eapc)`%** a year over the past 10 -- mostly in the colon, mostly at an advanced stage, and not because of neuroendocrine tumours, the appendix, screening, or more diagnosis of small tumours. This means that at the same age, people born since approximately 1960 have faced progressively higher colorectal cancer risk. Over 30 years deaths have not followed, which improved survival can explain; their fall over the past 10 years, while survival stood still, is a bit of a loose end.

After separating artefact from reality, the next step is to figure out what exposure is causing this. A rise in early-onset that is carried by birth cohorts, combined with cancer's long induction period, points to something in how the generations born since the 1960s grew up. Did some harmful exposure suddenly become much more prevalent? In the [ECCE project](https://ecce.iarc.who.int/), we are following up on promising evidence from the mutational signatures found in the colon of these people. Stay tuned!

```{r}
#| label: glance-check
#| include: false
# The numbers in the "At a glance" box are typed in, because the box comes
# before the data are read. A new download that moves them stops the render
# here, rather than leaving the box out of date.
eo <- "Early onset, 20-49"
glance <- c(
  eo_30      = trend_eapc("Incidence", eo, "Past 30 years")$eapc,
  eo_10      = trend_eapc("Incidence", eo, "Past 10 years")$eapc,
  colon_30   = band_eapc(inc$Colon, 5:10, "Past 30 years")$eapc,
  colon_10   = band_eapc(inc$Colon, 5:10, "Past 10 years")$eapc,
  rectum_30  = band_eapc(inc$Rectum, 5:10, "Past 30 years")$eapc,
  rectum_10  = band_eapc(inc$Rectum, 5:10, "Past 10 years")$eapc,
  stage4_30  = stage_eapc(eo, "IV", "Past 30 years")$eapc,
  men_30     = trend_eapc("Incidence", eo, "Past 30 years", "Men")$eapc,
  women_30   = trend_eapc("Incidence", eo, "Past 30 years", "Women")$eapc,
  men_10     = trend_eapc("Incidence", eo, "Past 10 years", "Men")$eapc,
  women_10   = trend_eapc("Incidence", eo, "Past 10 years", "Women")$eapc,
  stage4_10  = stage_eapc(eo, "IV", "Past 10 years")$eapc,
  stage1_30  = stage_eapc(eo, "I", "Past 30 years")$eapc,
  stage1_10  = stage_eapc(eo, "I", "Past 10 years")$eapc,
  mort_30    = trend_eapc("Mortality", eo, "Past 30 years")$eapc,
  mort_10    = trend_eapc("Mortality", eo, "Past 10 years")$eapc,
  mort_w_10  = trend_eapc("Mortality", eo, "Past 10 years", "Women")$eapc,
  mort_m_10  = trend_eapc("Mortality", eo, "Past 10 years", "Men")$eapc)
survival <- c(surv_at("18-44", "All", SURV_FROM), surv_at("18-44", "All", SURV_TO),
              surv_at("18-44", "All", 2005))
recent <- inc$`Colon and rectum` |> filter(sex == "Persons", year %in% 2020:2024)
share_50plus <- 100 * sum(recent$cases[recent$agegrp >= 11]) / sum(recent$cases)
cohorts <- c(inc  = 100 * (cohort_ratio("40-44", 1960, 1975)$rr - 1),
             mort = 100 * (cohort_ratio("40-44", 1960, 1975, d = ASPR$Mortality)$rr - 1))
stopifnot(
  "the EAPCs in the At a glance box no longer match the data" =
    all(round(glance, 1) == c(1.2, 1.0, 1.5, 2.3, 0.8, -1.0, 2.3,
                              1.3, 1.1, 1.4, 0.6, 1.1, 0.3, 0.5, -0.3, -1.6, -3.6, 0.3)),
  "the cohort gaps in the At a glance box no longer match the data" =
    all(round(cohorts) == c(40, 25)),
  "the survival in the At a glance box no longer matches the data" =
    all(round(survival) == c(55, 66, 67)),
  "the share of cases at 50 or older in the At a glance box no longer matches the data" =
    round(share_50plus) == 95,
  "the EAPCs with the NETs and the appendix in the At a glance box no longer match the data" =
    all(round(c(band_eapc(all_morph, 5:10, "Past 30 years")$eapc,
                band_eapc(all_morph, 5:10, "Past 10 years")$eapc), 1) == c(1.6, 1.4)),
  "stage I under 50 changed by more than the 'barely' of the At a glance box" =
    abs(stage_eapc(eo, "I", "Past 30 years")$eapc) < 0.5,
  "incidence at 50-74 is no longer below its 1989 level" =
    trend_at("Incidence", "Later onset, 50-74", 2024) <
    trend_at("Incidence", "Later onset, 50-74", 1989))
```
